trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Write at a Grade 8 reading level: sentences under 20 words, one idea per sentence, everyday words (use "help" not "facilitate", "check" not "verify", "customers" not "stakeholders", "start" not "commence"). Prefer short words with few syllables; avoid nouns ending in -tion, -ment, -isation where a verb will do. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: Junior Software Engineer (AI-Enabled)
Company: Ozow
About the company: Ozow is a leading fintech company that's redefining digital payments in South Africa and beyond. We're dedicated to making payments more accessible, secure, and convenient for both businesses and consumers. As a fast-growing player in the financial technology sector, Ozow fosters a culture of innovation, diversity, and inclusivity. We believe in pushing the boundaries of what's possible and are committed to making a positive impact on the world through our payment solutions.
Purpose of the role: Ozow is seeking a Junior Software Engineer (AI Enabled) to join our development team. You'll help build and maintain the solutions that power our digital payment platforms, learning from experienced engineers as we replatform and modernise our systems with AI. You'll use AI tools from day one, and we'll help you use them well: with discipline, care and an understanding of the code you ship. This is an early-career, hands-on engineering role, not an agentic AI role. Your focus is building software with AI, rather than designing autonomous, long-running agent workflows.
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - Work with cross-functional teams to build and maintain software solutions that meet high-quality standards and business requirements.
  - Contribute to replatforming existing systems onto modern, AI-native services, migrating well-defined pieces of functionality under the guidance of senior engineers.
  - Help build features that integrate with large language models (LLMs), learning techniques such as context management, embeddings and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
  - Write clean, efficient and maintainable code following our coding standards, using AI coding tools to learn and move faster while understanding and being able to explain everything you commit.
  - Follow the team's standards for using AI safely across the software development lifecycle, including checking AI-generated output and protecting sensitive and payment data.
  - Investigate and fix bugs and technical issues, escalating early when you're stuck.
  - Learn how our systems are designed for scalability, security and performance, and apply those principles in the features you build.
  - Take part in code reviews, both receiving feedback on your code and reviewing others' to build your understanding of the codebase.
  - Write unit tests for your code and help test features end to end, including AI features whose outputs are not always the same.
  - Learn and use our CI/CD pipelines, containers and cloud environments (AWS or Azure) to get your code safely into production.
  - Work in an Agile environment, participating in sprint planning, stand-ups and retrospectives.
  - Create and maintain technical documentation for the software and processes you work on.
  - Learn from senior engineers through pairing, code reviews and feedback, and share what you discover about using AI tools well with the wider team.
Must-have requirements:
  - 2 years of experience as a Software Engineer or Developer, including internships or graduate programmes
  - An IT Diploma or Degree, or equivalent practical experience such as a recognised coding bootcamp
  - Working knowledge of at least one of .NET C#, Python or JavaScript/ReactJs (more is a bonus)
  - Regular, thoughtful use of AI coding tools, with the ability to explain and check the code they produce
  - A good grasp of databases and SQL, version control (Git) and how the web works
  - A curious, pragmatic attitude towards AI and a strong willingness to learn
Nice-to-have:
  - Exposure to building with LLMs, for example through personal, university or work projects, beneficial
Location: Cape Town
Benefits:
  - Healthy breakfast, lunches and snacks
  - Monthly team connects
  - On-site Barista
  - Medical aid subsidy
  - Group Risk Insurance
  - Generous paid annual leave
  - Birthday leave
  - Learning and Development opportunities
  - Mentorship programme
  - Quarterly team building
  - Employee Assistance Programme (EAP)
  - Community initiatives
  - Access to cutting edge technology - Ozow Tech Stack
Application process: During the interview process you will meet with the People team, the hiring manager, and relevant CSuite. Our process may include psychometric and technical assessments, giving you an opportunity to demonstrate your strengths, skills and potential beyond your CV and interview.
How to apply / contact: Ready to be exceptional? Apply now! To find out more about life at Ozow, head over to our Careers Page here!
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.

Ozow

Cape Town

About us
Ozow is a leading fintech company that's redefining digital payments in South Africa and beyond. We're dedicated to making payments more accessible, secure, and convenient for both businesses and consumers. As a fast-growing player in the financial technology sector, Ozow fosters a culture of innovation, diversity, and inclusivity. We believe in pushing the boundaries of what's possible and are committed to making a positive impact on the world through our payment solutions.

About the role
Join our development team and help build the software behind our digital payment platforms. You will use AI tools from day one, and we will help you use them with care. You will learn from senior engineers as we replatform and modernise our systems. This is an early-career, hands-on engineering role. Your focus is building software with AI, not designing autonomous, long-running agent workflows.

Your team
You join our development team and learn from senior engineers through pairing, code reviews and feedback.

What you'll do
• Build and maintain software solutions with cross-functional teams, meeting our quality standards and business needs
• Help replatform existing systems onto modern, AI-native services by migrating well-defined pieces of functionality, guided by senior engineers
• Build features that work with large language models, learning context management, embeddings and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
• Write clean, efficient code that follows our coding standards, using AI coding tools to move faster while being able to explain everything you commit
• Follow team standards for safe AI use across the software development lifecycle, checking AI-generated output and protecting sensitive payment data
• Investigate and fix bugs and technical issues, and ask for help early when you are stuck
• Take part in code reviews, both getting feedback on your code and reviewing the code of others
• Write unit tests and help test features end to end, including AI features whose output can change
• Use our CI/CD pipelines, containers and cloud environments (AWS or Azure) to get code safely into production
• Work in an Agile team, joining sprint planning, stand-ups and retrospectives
• Create and keep up to date the technical documentation for the software and processes you work on
• Learn through pairing and feedback, and share what you discover about using AI tools well

What you need
• 2 years of experience as a Software Engineer or Developer, including internships or graduate programmes
• An IT Diploma or Degree, or equivalent practical experience such as a recognised coding bootcamp
• Working knowledge of at least one of .NET C#, Python or JavaScript/ReactJS
• Regular, thoughtful use of AI coding tools, with the ability to explain and check the code they produce
• A good grasp of databases and SQL, version control (Git) and how the web works
• A curious, practical attitude towards AI and a strong willingness to learn

Nice to have
• Experience building with LLMs, for example through personal, university or work projects
• Knowledge of more than one of .NET C#, Python or JavaScript/ReactJS

What we offer
• Healthy breakfast, lunches and snacks
• Monthly team connects
• On-site barista
• Medical aid subsidy
• Group Risk Insurance
• Generous paid annual leave
• Birthday leave
• Learning and development opportunities
• Mentorship programme
• Quarterly team building
• Employee Assistance Programme (EAP)
• Community initiatives
• Access to cutting edge technology - Ozow Tech Stack

How to apply
During the interview process you will meet with the People team, the hiring manager, and relevant C-Suite. The process may include psychometric and technical assessments. These give you a chance to show your strengths, skills and potential beyond your CV and interview.

To find out more about life at Ozow, head over to our Careers Page.
